title: feat(plugin-auth): with single sign-on configured, a signed-out visit can go straight to the identity provider and back, with a configurable local sign-in path
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoSLDKWQ8v7cxY9uDGijfncD)_

Fixes #33183

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — the new value is `requiresFeature: 'directSignIn'` on the `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` registry, a deployment setting surfaced to the page; no metadata author writes it today, and the operator docs (SSO page, environment-variable reference) teach it here

> **Contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER** (the face is schema: `packages/spec/src`). First pass FAIL (record 6879172654); delta PASS on `4fab4525` (record 6880597586) with two new should-fixes, F5 and F6, both addressed on this head; the same reviewer's delta on them is owed before landing.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：配置了单点登录的部署可以打开「直达登录」：未登录访问 Console 登录页时，直接跳到身份提供方，登录后回到原来要去的页面；本地密码登录入口可设为隐藏（`/login?local=1` 仍可进）或关闭。
- **为什么改**：只用一个身份提供方的企业，多一个登录页就是多一次点击和困惑；云端（C6）需要这个开关，自部署也能用。
- **风险与回滚**：默认关闭；不开时入口不挂载，`/auth/config` 只多一个 `directSignIn: false`；回滚只需关掉 `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_ENABLED`（或去掉 `directSignIn` 选项）。本地入口设为关闭时，登录表单在任何情况下都不提供本地登录方式；服务端密码登录接口不变，托管环境作废密码归 cloud#4471。
- **先看**：`direct-sign-in.ts`（回跳地址只留同源路径）和登录页的防循环判断 `directSignIn.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**：配一个 OIDC 提供方，设 `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_ENABLED=true`，退出后打开任意 Console 页面，应直接跳到提供方，登录后回到该页面；在提供方点拒绝，应停在登录页并显示原因和重试按钮，不会反复跳转；在 Console 里主动退出后，登录页停住并给出登录按钮，不会自动再跳；经身份提供方注销再回来时也一样（Tesla 裁决 6879236460）。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地（合约复审增量已 PASS；其新提的 F5、F6 已修，待同一复审者再做增量复审）。

## Ruling

Ruling 8 of cloud#4465 (the maintainer, 2026-11-13), as quoted on this issue in comment 6870716068:

> **Direct redirect to the identity provider is a platform feature, on by default in the cloud.**
> - The framework gains one setting: when SSO is configured, an unauthenticated visit skips the environment's sign-in page and goes straight to the configured identity provider, then returns to the original page.
> - The local sign-in path is configurable. Self-hosted can keep a hidden path (for example `/login?local=1`). Hosted has it off (ruling 10).
> - Self-hosted deployments with their own IdP can turn it on. Hosted environments have it on by default, with the cloud as the provider. The cloud sign-in page shows the organization's name and explains refusals (not a member under D5.1; invitation not accepted).

Ruling on the sign-out case (the maintainer, comment 6879236460 on this issue): after an explicit sign-out the sign-in page holds with a sign-in button; only a fresh signed-out visit starts on its own.

This PR is the framework half: the setting, the start door, the Console behaviour and the configurable local path. Turning it on by default for hosted environments, and the cloud sign-in page, are cloud#4471. Per D-2 (same comment), nothing here builds a recovery link or reopens the local path: with `localSignIn: 'off'` the sign-in form offers no local way in, in any of its states. `/register` and `/forgot-password` are unchanged pages.

**Not changed here:** the server's `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email` still accepts a password whatever `localSignIn` says (`off` is the page's choice). Invalidating hosted passwords (ruling 10) belongs to cloud#4471.

## What changes

**Server (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`).** A new setting, `directSignIn` on the auth plugin, with environment overrides that win field by field: `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_ENABLED`, `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_PROVIDER`, `OS_AUTH_DIRECT_SIGN_IN_LOCAL_PATH` (`hidden` | `off`; any other value refuses to boot).

- While it is on (read once at start-up from the auth manager's own setting, feature-detected like the neighbouring mounts), `GET /api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct?callbackURL=<path>` is mounted beside `/config`, before the auth wildcard, so a host forwarding `/api/v1/auth/*` gets it too. It picks the provider (the named one, or the one candidate across `oidcProviders` and `sys_sso_provider` rows), re-dispatches the vendor's own start (`/sign-in/social` for a generic-OAuth provider such as `objectstack-cloud`, `/sign-in/sso` for an SSO row) and answers 302 to the identity provider with the vendor's state cookie and `cache-control: no-store`. It mints nothing; the session is created by the vendor's callback as for any sign-in.
- The return path is kept only when it is a same-origin relative path at every percent-decoding layer (up to three): no `//`, no backslash, no control character, at most 2048 characters, and a URL parse that stays on the origin with a pathname that does not resolve to `//` (so `/..//host` and `/%2e%2e//host` are dropped). It is composed onto the canonical origin. A foreign path is dropped and the sign-in returns to the Console root. `errorCallbackURL` is always the Console `/login`.
- The query takes `callbackURL` only, once; an unknown or repeated parameter is refused 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` with the shared `@objectstack/rest` sentences, a name like `constructor` or `__proto__` included (the query is collected into an object with no prototype). No provider, several providers, a named provider that is not configured, or a refused start redirects to `/login?error=direct_sign_in_unavailable` with one `warn` line naming the reason. A start the vendor's sign-in rate limit refused (429; the vendor default of 3 per 10 seconds per address is kept) redirects to `/login?error=direct_sign_in_rate_limited` instead, reason `rate_limited`. A request that reaches the door after the setting was turned off answers 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
- `/auth/config` serves `features.directSignIn` always: `true` only while this server mounted the door and a provider can be started, so it never advertises a door that is not there (one source: the setting read at mount time). `features.localSignIn` is served while the setting is on.
- With the setting off the door is not mounted and every answer is as on `main`. `localSignIn: off` is the page's choice only: the password doors, `session.create.before` and `ssoOnlyMode` are untouched, so ADR-0135 D5.2 break-glass stays intact.

**Spec (`@objectstack/spec`).** `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` gains `directSignIn` (surface `login`, opt-in), so `requiresFeature` accepts the new value `requiresFeature: 'directSignIn'`. `localSignIn` joins the non-flag keys. `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema` gains both members. Regenerated: `references/api/auth-endpoints.mdx`, `references/data/object.mdx`, `references/ui/action.mdx`, `authorable-surface/api.json`.

**Console (`@object-ui/console`, `@object-ui/auth`, `@object-ui/i18n`).** With `features.directSignIn` on, the sign-in page sends a signed-out visitor to the door, returning to the same `/login` URL marked `direct=returned`, so the page's post-sign-in steps (organization pick, OAuth and mobile hand-offs, safe `?redirect=`) run as after any sign-in. The loop guard keeps the page drawn, with the reason and a **Continue with single sign-on** button, on an `error`, on a return without a session, and after an explicit sign-out in that tab (`sessionEndedBySignOut`, ruling 6879236460), also one that left through the identity provider's logout and came back as a full page load: `createAuthClient.signOut` writes a short note in the tab's `sessionStorage` just before following a provider-logout URL, the sign-out purge keeps it, and the first `AuthProvider` mount after the round trip starts with `sessionEndedBySignOut` raised and drops the note (honoured for ten minutes, read once, so a reload starts as a fresh visit). A rate-limited start has its own copy. An OAuth client's hand-off (`client_id` / `redirect_uri`) keeps today's page. `?local=1` draws today's page while the local path is `hidden` and is ignored while it is `off`. With `localSignIn: 'off'` the sign-in form (`@object-ui/auth` `LoginForm`) offers no local way in in any state that falls back to it: no email or phone form, no sign-up, no break-glass link, and no dev-admin row. That covers an OAuth client's hand-off and a deployment where no provider can start. Copy in all 11 locales.

**Docs.** A "Skip the sign-in page (direct sign-in)" section on the SSO page, and the three variables in the environment-variable reference.

## Tests

- `direct-sign-in.test.ts` (83): the setting and its env precedence; `keptReturnPath` over 22 foreign spellings (absolute, `//host`, `/\host`, `\\host`, `/%5cevil.example`, `/%2f%2f…`, double-encoded, an encoded scheme, `javascript:`, a tab or newline in the path, an encoded tab or newline, a broken escape, empty, over 2048 characters), each also through the door, where it returns to the Console root; the provider choice; the door with a fake host; the door mounted through `registerAuthRoutes` with the `objectstack-cloud` provider; both CONTROLs. New this round: the one-source describe composes the real `AuthPlugin` through `init()` with an `auth:configure` contribution and `registerAuthRoutes`, and pins that the door is mounted exactly when `/auth/config` advertises it (contribution: advertised and 302; no contribution CONTROL: `false` and 404; the setting turned on after the mount: still `false` and 404); a vendor 429 lands on `?error=direct_sign_in_rate_limited` with reason `rate_limited`; the 404 carries `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; the query refusals are the shared `@objectstack/rest` sentences; `/..//evil.example` and `/%2e%2e//evil.example` are dropped; `?constructor=1`, `?__proto__=1`, `?toString=1`, `?hasOwnProperty=1` and `?valueOf=1` are refused 400.
- `implicit-account-linking.test.ts` (+4 in a new describe): start → identity provider → callback over the real vendor, landing on the kept path with a session; a foreign return path lands on the Console root; an identity-provider error lands on `/_console/login?error=…`; a profile that cannot be read signs nobody in.
- `signOutRoundTrip-33183.test.tsx` in `@object-ui/auth` (9): the note is written before the provider-logout navigation and only then (CONTROL: an in-page sign-out, a failed sign-out); the sign-out purge keeps it; the first mount reads it raised and drops it; a reload, no note (CONTROL) and a stale note read lowered; a session on return lowers it.
- `LoginPage.direct-sign-in.test.tsx` (20): the decision table (with the `signedOut` rows), the start URL, and the page: CONTROL off, start, `?local=1` hidden vs off, the error hold with retry, the sessionless return, the OAuth hand-off, no local way in on the hand-off and on a refused start while the local path is off (with a CONTROL that `hidden` keeps the break-glass link), the door's `direct_sign_in_unavailable` copy, the rate-limited copy on the retry card, and, through the real `AuthProvider`, a signed-in visitor who signs out and lands on the page: it holds with the sign-in button and does not navigate (ruling 6879236460); and the real client's sign-out answered with a provider-logout URL, then a fresh load of the page: it holds, and a reload starts.
- Pins updated: the public feature count (14 → 15) and the served `/auth/config` fixture in `@objectstack/spec`; the exact `features` pin in `auth-manager.test.ts`; the auth route ledger's objectstack-mount pin and the `handleRequest` surface test (which now composes the door), with a reviewed `public` row for `GET /api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct`. The door's 404 uses the registered `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, so the error-code ledger is unchanged.

## Acceptance notes

Each pin was ablated with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the mutation verified on disk, the restore verified against HEAD) and went red:

| Pin | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 round trip | the door ignores the kept path | 2 failed |
| 2 open redirect | drop the `//` check / the backslash check / the control-character check / the decode layers | 7 / 5 / 8 / 16 failed |
| 2 open redirect | keep any string as the return path | 51 failed |
| 2 open redirect | keep any string and drop the same-origin backstop on the composed URL | 52 failed |
| 3 local hidden vs off | honour `?local=1` while off | 2 failed |
| 4 no loop | do not hold on `error` / on `direct=returned` | 2 / 2 failed |
| 5 CONTROL off | mount the door with the setting off / start on the page without the flag | 52 / 3 failed |
| 6 CONTROL api, mcp, bearer | the door claims every GET | 1 failed |
| 7 local off on the form | `LoginForm` ignores `localSignIn: 'off'` | 2 failed |
| 8 one source (F1) | `/auth/config` advertises without the mounted flag | 1 failed |
| 9 rate limited (F4) | drop the 429 branch | 1 failed |
| 10 hold after sign-out (F2) | drop the `signedOut` decision / the page passes `signedOut: false` | 2 / 1 failed |
| 11 `//` after resolution (N4) | drop the resolved-pathname check | 4 failed |
| 12 prototype names (F5) | collect the query into a plain `{}` | 5 failed |
| 13 provider-logout hold (F6) | no note written / not read on mount / not dropped on mount / swept by the purge / no age window | 3 / 2 / 3 / 1 / 1 failed |

One layer did not go red alone: the URL-parse origin check inside `keptReturnPath`. It is a backstop by construction: a path that passes the `//`, backslash and control-character checks at every decode layer resolves on the origin, so no input reaches that check alone. The resolved-pathname check beside it (row 11) does go red alone, on dot segments that collapse to `//`.

Open-redirect cases covered, each dropped and never followed: absolute (`https://evil.example/x`, `http://evil.example`), protocol-relative (`//evil.example`), backslash (`/\evil.example`, `\\evil.example`, `/%5cevil.example`, `/%5Cevil.example`), encoded slashes (`/%2f%2f…`, double-encoded `/%252f%252f…`), an encoded scheme (`https%3A%2F%2Fevil.example`), `javascript:`, a tab or newline in the path (raw and encoded), a broken escape, empty and over-long values.

Both CONTROLs hold: with the setting off the door is not mounted and `/auth/config` differs only by `directSignIn: false`; with it on, `/api/*`, `/mcp`, API-key and bearer requests are never redirected.
